acceptance.output_evidence:
RECORDED FOR L9, NO VERDICT.
1. THE CLOSED DAY WAS TOLD APART FROM A HOLE, ON REAL DATA. The deployed classifier's verdict for 2026-09, written by EG-s-15's run at 2026-09-10T01:20:20Z, beside the calendar:
    partner       A  COVERED  B  C  D  UNKNOWN  trading_days  holes        coverage_line
    49financial   3  5        0  0  1  0        6             ['2026-09-09'] 5/6 trading days; 1 carried
    inflection    3  6        0  0  0  0        6             []             6/6 trading days; 0 carried
    cottonwood    3  5        0  0  1  0        6             ['2026-09-09'] 5/6 trading days; 1 carried
  THE CALENDAR BESIDE IT (lib/trading_calendar.py, is_trading_day, measured this session): 09-01 Tue True, 09-02 Wed True, 09-03 Thu True, 09-04 Fri True, 09-05 Sat FALSE, 09-06 Sun FALSE, 09-07 Mon FALSE (Labor Day), 09-08 Tue True, 09-09 Wed True. Six trading days and THREE non-trading -- and every partner's A == 3 and trading_days == 6. The classifier and the calendar agree exactly, on real data, for 3 of 3 partners. 2026-09-07 is in NO partner's holes, and each hole list is identical with the date removed. The only holes in the month are 2026-09-09, class D, on 49financial and cottonwood -- a genuinely absent upstream partition, not a closed market. THE RULE, quoted: classifier.py:122-125 @c866edd324 'if not tcal.is_trading_day(d): result[date_str] = {"class": "A", "reason": "market closed (not a trading day)"}; continue'.
2. WAS ANYTHING BACKFILLED AGAINST IT? SPLIT ANSWER, and this is the finding. For the two partners the criterion enumerates: NO -- daily/cottonwood/ 0 of 62 keys and daily/49financial/ 0 of 89 keys name 2026-09-07, no key under either prefix was modified during the run window, and neither producer's log group carries a line naming the date (14 and 11 lines scanned). FOR THE THIRD PARTNER, WHICH THE CRITERION DOES NOT ENUMERATE: YES -- daily/inflection/2026-09-07.json exists, 1209 B, written 2026-09-07T15:00:41Z, carrying four priced ETF rows with account_count 562 and source_as_of 2026-09-07, citing s3://opal-data-inf/gold/canonical/holdings_2026-09-07.parquet. inflection also has 09-05 (Sat) and 09-06 (Sun), and a sha256 over each file's (ticker, ownership_value, account_count) tuples is IDENTICAL across 09-05, 09-06, 09-07 and 09-08 while DIFFERING from 09-04 -- carried-forward duplicates, not independently priced days. Note this was NOT written by EG-s-15's run (its LastModified is 09-07, three days before), so it is standing behaviour of inflection's own producer, not an act of the run this order reads. Row W1-S31.
3. WHERE THE ROUND-1 FIXTURE PROOFS WOULD HAVE BEEN BLIND, three places. (i) A fixture supplies its own calendar answer, so it can only confirm that a date the fixture CALLS non-trading is classified A; it cannot confirm that the real calendar calls 2026-09-07 non-trading, which is the half that matters for a real holiday (a weekend is easy; a moveable federal holiday is where a calendar is actually tested). (ii) A fixture asserts the classifier's OUTPUT and therefore cannot notice that the PERSISTED verdict drops the per-date class map -- the gap this order hit in arms (b)/(c) and filed as W1-S30 -- because a fixture reads the in-memory dict, not the served object. (iii) A fixture builds only the partners it names, so it cannot surface a partner whose producer writes on closed days; that required listing the real prefixes, and it is exactly what the criterion's own 2-of-3 enumeration also misses. THE STRUCTURAL BLINDNESS BEHIND (iii), quoted: the class-A branch at classifier.py:122-125 @c866edd324 `continue`s BEFORE the `if date_str in series` slice check at :128 -- so the classifier never examines whether a slice exists on a non-trading day, for any partner, in any month. A check scoped to trading days cannot see a defect on the non-trading ones.
4. WHAT THIS ORDER COULD NOT SEE. (i) Whether daily/inflection/2026-09-07.json is INTENDED (a deliberate carry-forward in inflection's feed) or a defect -- inflection's producer is outside this project's surface and this worker does not assert which. (ii) The BEFORE state of the daily prefixes: no listing predates EG-s-15's run and a prefix listing is not retrospective, so the before-state is an inference from 0 keys now plus nothing modified in the window, and is labelled so. (iii) S3 object-level PutObject on opal-data-etfs -- COVERAGE-ABSENT, no data-event selector covers the bucket and versioning is disabled (W1-S12), so every write question is answered from the object and the producer's log instead. (iv) Which dates the run classified A: the served verdict carries counts, not a per-date map (W1-S30).

The discriminator is the POSITIVE CONTROL the face names: 2026-09-08 is a trading day, and it must behave differently from 2026-09-07 on every instrument. It does: the calendar answers True vs False; the daily prefixes carry a 2026-09-08 slice for BOTH enumerated partners (1345 B and 1305 B) and ZERO for 2026-09-07. A second, independent control on the same claim: the month's ONLY holes are 2026-09-09 (class D) -- so the verdict demonstrably CAN mark a date a hole, and did, three days after the target; the absence of 09-07 from the hole lists is therefore a reading and not an inability to report holes. THIRD, on the count: the A count was checked against an INDEPENDENTLY measured calendar rather than assumed -- 3 non-trading days measured, A == 3 in the artifact, for 3 of 3 partners; had the count been 2 or 4 the arm would have failed.

determinism.method: READ-ONLY by the order's BOUNDS and by Andrew's standing constraint: no invoke, no write, no deploy, and in particular NO invocation of etfs-reports-orchestrator in any mode that can reach _email_report. Every read is idempotent and re-runnable: s3api list-objects-v2 / head-object / get-object, logs filter-log-events over FIXED ms bounds, and a pure function call into lib/trading_calendar.py. The battery was run twice this session (once with a defective timestamp parser in arm (f), once after fixing it); every measured number was identical across both runs and only the arm-(f) verdict changed.
determinism.observed: Run 1 and run 2 agree on all data: 3 non-trading days; A=3 for 3 of 3 partners; 0 occurrences of the literal date in the verdict; 0 of 62 and 0 of 89 daily keys; 1 of 122 for inflection; 14 and 11 producer log lines. Arm (f) moved FAIL -> PASS purely because of an instrument bug in this battery, not a change in the world: s3api head-object renders LastModified in RFC-1123 ('Thu, 10 Sep 2026 01:20:20 GMT') while list-objects-v2 renders ISO-8601, and the first parser branched on `"T" in value`, which matches the 'T' of 'Thu' and truncated the string. Fixed by discriminating on SHAPE (positions of '-' and 'T'), and the note is left in the battery's source so the next reader does not repeat it.
